payload.goal: Reconcile the attached bank statement CSV against open customer and supplier invoices in Tripletex, matching incoming and outgoing payments and handling partial payments correctly.
success_checks: All bank statement lines from the CSV are imported or represented in reconciliation workflow
Incoming payments are matched to the correct customer invoices: 1001, 1002, 1003, 1004, 1005
Outgoing payments to suppliers Martins Lda, Pereira Lda, and Costa Lda are matched to the correct supplier invoices or flagged for manual review
Partial payments are applied without overpaying invoices and remaining balances stay open
Unmatched lines such as interest, tax withholding, and bank fee are posted or flagged appropriately
Bank account balance movement in Tripletex aligns with the statement lines processed
risk_notes: Sandbox is empty, so invoices/suppliers/customers/bank account may need to be created before reconciliation can be completed

CSV provides invoice numbers only for customer receipts; supplier payment lines do not include supplier invoice numbers, so exact matching may require amount/date/vendor inference or manual confirmation
No opening bank balance/account number/currency provided
Line 'Bankgebyr' has amount in the 'Inn' column though it appears to be a fee; sign/direction may need validation before posting
Tax withholding and interest income may require ledger posting rules/accounts not specified in prompt
If open invoices in Tripletex do not exist or amounts differ, automatic reconciliation will fail

ordered_steps: Create or verify bank account/cash account in Tripletex for reconciliation target
Parse CSV attachment into dated bank transactions with amount direction and reference text
Search Tripletex open customer invoices by invoice numbers 1001, 1002, 1003, 1004, 1005
If sandbox lacks those invoices, bootstrap prerequisites: create customers -> create orders -> add order lines -> create invoices with matching invoice numbers/amounts if possible
Match incoming transactions to customer invoices by invoice number and amount; register full or partial payments on invoice endpoints
Search Tripletex open supplier invoices for Martins Lda, Pereira Lda, and Costa Lda by supplier, amount, and nearby due/payment dates
If sandbox lacks suppliers/invoices, bootstrap prerequisites: create suppliers -> register supplier invoices with matching open amounts where confirmed
Match outgoing transactions to supplier invoices and register payments; if multiple open invoices exist, apply partial payment logic and leave residual open balance

Run final bank reconciliation check to ensure all statement lines are matched, posted, or explicitly left unresolved with reason

rules: Use params={"number": XXXX} to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
This is a QUERY PARAM via the params field — NOT json_body.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isSupplier (it's readOnly).
ALWAYS include phoneNumber if provided in the prompt — scoring checks phone.
ALWAYS include postalAddress with addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161} when address info is provided.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Method is PUT, not POST.
ALL params are QUERY PARAMETERS — NOT in body: PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment?paymentDate=YYYY-MM-DD&paymentTypeId=XXXXX&paidAmount=YYYYY
Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType — use the first result's id.
paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.
ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
AUTO-SPLIT RULES: ONLY vatType id=3 (25% utgående) triggers auto-split. vatType id=1 does NOT auto-split.
For supplier costs: use vatType=3 (NOT id=1) with ONLY the debit posting. Tripletex detects the expense account and applies inngående MVA automatically.
For vatType=0: include BOTH debit AND credit postings manually. They must sum to 0.
If you get 422 'postings don't sum to 0': switch to vatType=3 with single debit posting, OR add both debit+credit with vatType=0.
NEVER use vatType=1 — it does NOT auto-generate balancing entries and will always cause 422 with single posting.
Do NOT include currency on postings — let it default. Including currency={} causes 'factor must be >= 1' error.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
Resolve account numbers: GET /ledger/account with params={"number": XXXX}, then use account={"id": resolved_id}. NEVER use account={"number": XXXX} in postings.

what_went_wrong: Critical $REF alias resolution failure: PUT /ledger/account used '$REF:account_1920' as path parameter ID, causing 422 error and blocking bank account setup.
Agent ran out of budget/steps before completing core reconciliation: no invoices were created via /invoice, no payments registered via PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment.
SEMANTIC BLOCKED on Silva Lda order line (amount mismatch 6450 vs 8062.5), halting that invoice creation mid-flow.
Wrong approach: agent created orders/orderlines instead of directly creating invoices, wasting calls and never reaching the payment registration step.
what_worked: Agent correctly identified all bank statement transactions and matched amounts to customers/suppliers.
Existing customers and payment types were successfully discovered via GET calls.
what_to_try_next: Resolve account ID before PUT: first GET /ledger/account to extract numeric ID, then use that integer directly in PUT /ledger/account/{id} path — never use $REF in path params.
Skip order/orderline bootstrap entirely; use POST /invoice directly with customer, date, and amount to create invoices faster within budget.
After creating invoices, immediately call PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment with correct paymentTypeId and amount to register each payment, including partial payments for invoices 1002 and 1004.
unnecessary_calls: POST /order (x5) — creating orders is unnecessary; invoices can be created directly via POST /invoice without orders
POST /order/orderline (x4) — orderlines are redundant if invoices are created directly
GET /invoice/paymentType — useful but could be deferred until payment registration step to save early budget
